import sqlite3

# Connect to the database
conn = sqlite3.connect('./data.db')
cursor = conn.cursor()

# Execute SQL query to compute ratio_sql using integer division
query = """
SELECT 
    numerator,
    denominator,
    CASE 
        WHEN denominator = 0 THEN NULL
        ELSE numerator // denominator
    END AS ratio_sql
FROM your_table_name;
"""

cursor.execute(query)
results = cursor.fetchall()

# Display the results
for row in results:
    print(row)

# Close the connection
conn.close()

cursor = conn.cursor()

# Get table names
cursor.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table';")
tables = cursor.fetchall()
print("Tables in database:", tables)

# If there are tables, check the structure of the first one
if tables:
    cursor.execute(f"PRAGMA table_info({tables[0][0]})")
    columns = cursor.fetchall()
    print(f"\nColumns in {tables[0][0]}:")

        print(col)

conn.close()

import pandas as pd
import sqlite3

# Connect to the database and read the tables
conn = sqlite3.connect('./data.db')

# Read the purchase_price table
purchase_price_df = pd.read_sql_query("SELECT * FROM purchase_price", conn)

# Read the product_loss table
product_loss_df = pd.read_sql_query("SELECT * FROM product_loss", conn)

# Merge the dataframes on Item Code
merged_df = pd.merge(purchase_price_df, product_loss_df, on='Item Code', how='inner')

# Compute ratio_py using Python division
merged_df['ratio_py'] = merged_df['Purchase Price'] * (1 + merged_df['Loss Rate (%)'] / 100)

# Compute ratio_sql using SQL query
ratio_sql_query = """
SELECT 
    pp."Item Code",
    pp."Purchase Price",
    pl."Loss Rate (%)",
    pp."Purchase Price" * (1 + pl."Loss Rate (%)" / 100) as ratio_sql
FROM purchase_price pp
JOIN product_loss pl ON pp."Item Code" = pl."Item Code"
"""
ratio_sql_df = pd.read_sql_query(ratio_sql_query, conn)

# Merge the SQL results back for comparison
comparison_df = pd.merge(merged_df, ratio_sql_df[['Item Code', 'ratio_sql']], on='Item Code')

# Compare the two ratios
comparison_df['difference'] = comparison_df['ratio_py'] - comparison_df['ratio_sql']
comparison_df['match'] = comparison_df['difference'].abs() < 1e-10

print("Comparison of ratio_py and ratio_sql:")
print(comparison_df[['Item Code', 'Item Name', 'Purchase Price', 'Loss Rate (%)', 'ratio_py', 'ratio_sql', 'match']])

# Check if all values match
all_match = comparison_df['match'].all()
print(f"\nAll ratios match: {all_match}")

conn.close()

import sqlite3
import pandas as pd

# Connect to the database
conn = sqlite3.connect('./data.db')

# Read both tables into DataFrames
purchase_df = pd.read_sql_query("SELECT * FROM purchase_price", conn)
loss_df = pd.read_sql_query("SELECT * FROM product_loss", conn)

# Check for matching Item Codes
purchase_codes = set(purchase_df['Item Code'].unique())
loss_codes = set(loss_df['Item Code'].unique())

print(f"Item Codes in purchase_price: {len(purchase_codes)}")
print(f"Item Codes in product_loss: {len(loss_codes)}")
print(f"Intersection: {len(purchase_codes.intersection(loss_codes))}")
print(f"Only in purchase_price: {purchase_codes - loss_codes}")
print(f"Only in product_loss: {loss_codes - purchase_codes}")

# Merge the data to see all values side by side
merged_df = pd.merge(purchase_df, loss_df, on='Item Code', how='inner', suffixes=('_purchase', '_loss'))
print(f"\nNumber of matching rows: {len(merged_df)}")

# Show sample of merged data
print("\nSample merged data (first 5 rows):")
print(merged_df.head())

conn.close()
